instructions: gowhatsapp is a zero-third-party-dependency Go client for the official WhatsApp Cloud API (Meta Graph API): sending text/media/template/interactive messages and receiving webhooks. Single module, stdlib-only core (net/http, crypto/hmac, encoding/json). Prioritize the security-sensitive paths (webhook signature verification, secret handling), API-compatibility guarantees (the sealed Message interface, the Doer transport seam), and retry/context correctness over style. See DESIGN.md for architecture and API-stability policy, SECURITY.md for the secret-handling contract, and .greptile/rules.md for pattern rationale drawn from this repo's own past review (REVIEW.md).

rules.rule: This library ships zero third-party dependencies in its core module (only net/http, crypto/hmac, encoding/json, etc. from the standard library). Flag any new non-stdlib import added to a root-module file; a dependency belongs in a caller's application, not here.

Message is sealed via an unexported buildRequest method so only this package can implement it (message.go, template.go, interactive.go). Adding a new message type must stay purely additive — never change buildRequest's signature, never export it, and never require existing callers to change code. This is the library's core non-breaking-change guarantee per DESIGN.md section 3.3.

Every error the client returns must wrap one of the sentinels in errors.go (errors.Is must work). A new Cloud API error code must be added to classify()'s switch, mapped to the most specific existing sentinel or left unmapped (nil) to fall back to ErrTransient/ErrSendFailed — never introduce a bespoke error string a caller would have to substring-match. Preserve the *int Code field in parseAPIError's json envelope (not int) — it exists specifically so an absent code is distinguishable from a real code of 0, which would otherwise be misclassified as ErrUnauthorized.

X-Hub-Signature-256 verification must remain a constant-time comparison (hmac.Equal), never ==, bytes.Equal on attacker-influenced data compared byte-by-byte in a way that could short-circuit, or any other early-exit comparison. An empty AppSecret intentionally disables verification for local testing — do not silently change that default without flagging it as a security-relevant behavior change.

AccessToken, AppSecret, and raw webhook signatures must never be logged, included in an error message, or exposed through String()/Error() methods. APIError's FBTraceID and Code are the safe fields for diagnostics per SECURITY.md — anything else derived from a request/response that could carry the token or secret needs explicit scrubbing before it reaches a log line or error string.

The retry loop in transport.go must sleep at exactly one point per iteration, carrying the computed delay (from Retry-After or exponential backoff) forward into the top-of-loop wait — never sleep once inside an error branch and again at the top of the next iteration. This exact double-sleep bug (a 429 with Retry-After honored, then an extra backoff on top, while the network-error path only slept once) was found and fixed via TestSend_RetryBackoffNotDoubled; see .greptile/rules.md.

Upload buffers the caller's entire io.Reader into memory before sending (documented behavior, not yet capped) and Download returns the full media body as a []byte with no explicit size limit of its own. A change that adds another unbounded io.ReadAll/bytes.Buffer accumulation of caller- or network-supplied data should either reuse an existing cap (like webhook.go's http.MaxBytesReader) or call out why one isn't needed.
Every network-calling method must accept and honor context.Context, including mid-retry (sleepCtx must return ctx.Err() promptly on cancellation rather than sleeping to completion first).
Every new or newly-exported type, function, method, and constant must have a doc comment that starts with the identifier's own name.
